title: Modi Flags Off India's First Hydrogen-Powered Train on Haryana's Jind-Sonipat Route
excerpt: The 10-coach, 2,600-passenger trainset emits only water vapour and puts India in the same league as Germany, Japan, and China in hydrogen rail technology.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi on July 17 flagged off India's first hydrogen-powered passenger train, running the 89-km Jind-Sonipat route in Haryana with zero carbon emissions.
  • The 10-coach trainset, dubbed 'Namo Green Rail,' carries 2,600 passengers and is powered by a 1,200-kilowatt hydrogen fuel cell system producing 3,200 horsepower — making it one of the world's most powerful hydrogen trains.
  • India joins a select group of countries operating hydrogen rail services, including Germany, Japan, China, and the United States.
  • The train was designed, engineered, and built entirely in India, with a dedicated 3,000-kg hydrogen storage and refuelling facility at Jind station.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday flagged off India's first hydrogen-powered passenger train from Jind railway station in Haryana, marking a milestone in the country's push toward decarbonising one of the world's largest rail networks. The train will run twice daily on the 89-kilometre route to Sonipat, stopping at 12 intermediate stations, with a journey time of approximately two hours.

How It Works

The trainset, styled in a distinctive sky-blue and white livery and named 'Namo Green Rail,' is powered by Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFC) that convert compressed hydrogen into electricity. The only by-products are water vapour and heat — no carbon dioxide, no particulate matter, no diesel fumes.

At 3,200 horsepower from a 1,200-kilowatt fuel cell system, the train is one of the most powerful hydrogen-powered passenger trainsets operating anywhere in the world, according to Indian Railways. Its 10-coach configuration also makes it among the longest. The maximum operating speed is 75 km/h, with a design speed of 110 km/h.

"The project combines advanced propulsion technology with dedicated hydrogen storage, refuelling and operational infrastructure."

— Government of India statement

Why It Matters

India has electrified nearly all of its 70,000-km broad-gauge network — one of the world's largest — in pursuit of net-zero carbon emissions in railways by 2030, according to Reuters. But electrification requires continuous overhead wiring, which is impractical or uneconomical on certain routes. Hydrogen trains fill that gap: they generate electricity onboard, eliminating the need for overhead catenary infrastructure while remaining emission-free.

The launch places India in a small club of nations operating hydrogen-powered rail services. Germany pioneered the technology with the Alstom Coradia iLint in 2018. Japan, China, and the United States have since introduced their own variants. India's entry is notable for its scale — at 2,600-passenger capacity, it exceeds most existing hydrogen trainsets globally.

Built in India, for India

The trainset was designed, engineered, and integrated entirely in India by the Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO) under Indian Railways. A dedicated 3,000-kilogram hydrogen storage and refuelling facility has been constructed at Jind station, with 24/7 monitoring and comprehensive safety systems including leak, flame, smoke, and heat detection.

Modi described the launch as a landmark moment for Indian Railways and a strong example of the Make in India initiative. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, Haryana Governor Ashim Kumar Ghosh, and Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini attended the ceremony. School children were among the first passengers aboard the inaugural run.

"India would continue to find ways to improve efficiency, reduce costs and expand the network."

— Prime Minister Narendra Modi, after flagging off the train

The Diaspora Connection

For the Indian diaspora, particularly those in countries where hydrogen rail is already operational, the launch signals India's growing technological ambition. The train supports the National Green Hydrogen Mission, which aims to position India as a global hub for green hydrogen production and consumption — a sector that could generate significant investment and employment opportunities in the coming decade.

What's Next

The Jind-Sonipat route will serve as a pilot. If the trial delivers the expected operational and commercial results, Indian Railways is likely to consider hydrogen-powered services on additional routes where full electrification is not viable. Modi said the hydrogen rail infrastructure would also create opportunities for new industries and jobs.

The launch was part of a broader package of development projects worth approximately ₹14,700 crore ($1.75 billion) that Modi inaugurated in Haryana on the same day, spanning highways, medical colleges, and cultural infrastructure.
